paragraphs: § Ignoring God Leads to a Downward Spiral

This is Paul, and I'm on a mission for Jesus Christ. He's the real MVP, and I'm his devoted servant—his hand-picked messenger, chosen to spread the word about God's awesome power. I'm writing this to all of you in Rome who are on God's team—you belong to Jesus because he called you.

So, the ancient prophets were already dropping hints about God's Son, Jesus. He was a real guy, a descendant of King David, so he's got street cred. But his transformation was insane. When God raised him from the dead, the Holy Spirit flexed his power and showed everyone that Jesus is the Son of God, the Messiah, our ultimate boss. Because of him, we got this amazing gift of a new life and a super important job: to tell everyone else about it so they can trust and follow him too. You guys are part of this because Jesus called you. So, I'm sending you all the positive energy from God our Father and our main man, Jesus.

First off, I gotta thank God—through Jesus—for every single one of you. Seriously, people everywhere are talking about how strong your faith is, and it gets me hyped every time I hear it. God knows I'm not faking it; I worship and serve him by spreading the good news about his Son. I'm constantly praying for you guys, asking him to make a way for me to finally come and visit. The longer I have to wait, the more I want to be there to share some of God's gifts with you in person and see you level up in your faith. But don't get it twisted, I'm not just coming to give. I know you've got plenty to teach me too. It's a two-way street.

And hey, don't think I've been ignoring you. I've tried to get to Rome so many times, but something always gets in the way. I really want to see God do some cool stuff with you guys, just like I've seen in other places. I feel like I owe it to everyone—smart or not, from the city or not, no matter who they are—to share this message. That's why I'm so pumped to finally come to Rome and tell you all about the good news of God.

I'm not ashamed of this message. It's God's power in action, a rescue plan for everyone who trusts in him. It started with the Jews, but now it's for everybody. God's way of making things right is all about faith, from start to finish. Just like the old scriptures say, "The one who is right with God by faith will truly live."

But here's the deal: God is not happy. He's seriously furious about all the messed-up stuff people do to ignore the truth. The truth about God is right in front of your face. Just look around at everything he's made! You can see his incredible power and his divine nature. So, no one has an excuse. People knew who God was, but they didn't treat him like the boss. They started acting like fools and got all confused. They thought they were so smart, but they were clueless about what really matters. They traded the glory of the all-powerful God for some cheap, knock-off statues you could buy at a garage sale.

So, God was like, "Fine, have it your way." And before they knew it, they were living in their own filth, inside and out. They chose a fake god over the real God, and they started worshiping the things they made instead of the one who made them. But we know who the real God is, and he's the one who blesses us. Amen to that!

And it got even worse. Since they refused to acknowledge God, they forgot how to be human. They got all mixed up, and their relationships became a total mess. It was all about lust, not love. And they paid the price for it, big time. They were empty, without God and without love—just a bunch of sad, lonely people.

Since they couldn't be bothered with God, he let them do their own thing. And all hell broke loose. They were evil, greedy, and always stabbing each other in the back. They made life a living nightmare with their jealousy, violence, and cheating. They were mean, awful, and always talking trash about God. They were bullies and show-offs, always bragging about themselves. They kept finding new ways to ruin people's lives and even turned on their own parents. They were foolish, heartless, and cruel. And the craziest part is, they knew it was wrong. They knew they were spitting in God's face, but they didn't care. Even worse, they cheered on the people who were the best at being the worst.

paragraphs: § God Is Kind, but Not Soft

So you think you're hot stuff, pointing fingers at everyone else? Think again. Every time you roast someone, you're actually roasting yourself. It's like, "takes one to know one," you know? You're just trying to distract from your own mess, but God sees right through that. He's not falling for your smoke and mirrors; he knows what you've been up to.

You didn't actually think you could fool God, did you? Like, just because he's a nice guy, he'll let you off the hook? Nah, you better rethink that. God is kind, for sure, but he's not soft. He'll grab your hand and pull you into an amazing change, a complete life change.

You're not getting away with anything. Every time you walk away from God, you're just adding fuel to the fire. And one day, that fire is gonna blaze, and God's righteous judgment will come down. Make no mistake, you'll get what's coming to you. If you're on God's team, you get the ultimate prize: real life. But if you're stubborn and do your own thing, you're gonna get burned.

If you mess up, you're gonna get splinters, no matter where you're from or who your parents are. But if you roll with God, you'll get awesome rewards, no matter your background. Being a Jew doesn't give you an automatic stamp of approval. God doesn't care what other people say about you; he makes up his own mind.

If you mess up without knowing it, God gets that. But if you mess up and you know exactly what you're doing, that's a whole different story. Just hearing God's rules is a waste of time if you don't actually do them. It's the doing that matters to God.

When people who've never even heard of God's law instinctively follow it, they're showing that the law is written on their hearts. They have a built-in sense of right and wrong. And on judgment day, everyone's gonna see how they responded to that inner voice. The message I'm spreading through Jesus takes all of that into account.
§ Religion Can't Save You

And for all you who grew up in the church, don't think you can just chill and take it easy. Don't get cocky because you know all the right answers. I'm talking to you, Mr. Know-It-All, who thinks he can guide everyone else. Who's guiding you? Seriously. You're telling people not to steal while you're robbing them blind? You're talking about being faithful while you're cheating? You can get away with a lot if you talk a good game, but people see right through that. It's because of you that people who don't know God roll their eyes at him.

Being circumcised is a big deal if you're living God's way. But if you're not, it's meaningless. And if someone who isn't circumcised lives God's way, that's better than being circumcised and not. It's better to keep God's law uncircumcised than to break it circumcised. See, it's not about what's on the outside that makes you a real Jew. It's about what's in your heart. It's God's mark on you, not some physical mark, that counts. And that's the only recognition that matters.

paragraphs: Okay, so what makes Jewish people special? Or what's the point of all the religious rules? It matters, big time.

They were the ones who got to be the keepers of God's message. Depend on it: God keeps his word even when the whole world is lying through its teeth. Scripture says the same: "Your words stand fast and true; rejection doesn't faze you." But seriously, does our messing up make God unfaithful? Not at all. God's truth doesn't depend on us being good. But wait, if our wrongdoing only underlines and confirms God's rightdoing, shouldn't we get a little credit for helping out? The answer to that is no—a most emphatic no! How else would things ever get straightened out if God didn't do the straightening?

It's simply perverse to say, 'If my lies make God's truth look even more glorious, why blame me? I'm doing God a favor.' Some people have the audacity to claim that we go around saying, 'Let's do more bad stuff so God can do more good!' Uh, that's pure slander, and I'm sure you'd agree.
§ We're All in the Same Sinking Boat
So, are we Jews better than everyone else? Not really. The truth is, we're all in the same boat. We're all sinners. The Scriptures are crystal clear about it:

> Nobody's living right, not even one.
> Nobody gets it, nobody's even looking for God.
> Everyone took a wrong turn;
> everyone's wandering down dead-end alleys.
> No one's living right;
> I can't find a single one.
> Their words are like open graves,
> their tongues slippery as mud.
> Everything they say has a little poison in it.
> They open their mouths and the air gets toxic.
> They're racing to be the worst of the worst,
> leaving a trail of heartbreak and wreckage.
> They don't know the first thing about getting along with people.
> They never give God the time of day.

See? The Scriptures aren't just talking about other people; they're talking to us. We're all sinners, and we're all in this together. Knowing God's rules doesn't make us right with him. It just shows us how much we've messed up, just like everyone else.
§ God Has Set Things Right

But now, God has a new plan. It's what Moses and the prophets were talking about all along. God is making things right, and he's doing it through Jesus. This isn't just for us; it's for everyone who believes in him. It doesn't matter who you are or what you've done. We've all messed up and fallen short of God's glorious plan for our lives. But God, in his amazing generosity, decided to give us a fresh start. It's a total gift. He rescued us from the mess we were in and put us back on track. And he did it all through Jesus Christ.

God sent Jesus as a sacrifice to wipe out the world's sin. When we have faith in him, we're made right with God. God did this for everyone to see, to show that he's a just God who deals with sin. He's not just sweeping it under the rug. He's dealing with it head-on, right now, in our time. God makes things right, and he makes it possible for us to live in his rightness.

So, what happened to all our bragging about being God's chosen people? It's been canceled. We've learned that God doesn't care about what we do; he cares about what he does. We finally get it. We're in sync with God when we let him lead, not when we're trying to be the star of the show.

And what about our claim that we have a special connection to God? That's been canceled too. God is the God of everyone, not just the Jews. There's only one God, and he makes things right for everyone who trusts in him, whether they follow all the religious rules or have never even heard of them.

But does this mean we can just forget about all the rules and commands God gave us? Not at all. When we focus on what God has done, we're actually showing how important those rules are. We're putting them in their proper place and showing that they all point to him.

paragraphs: § Trusting God

So, let's talk about Abraham, like, the founding father of our whole faith thing. How does he fit into all this? If Abraham got on God's good side by doing a bunch of stuff, he'd have some serious bragging rights. But the Bible isn't about Abraham's highlight reel; it's about God's master plan. Scripture says, "Abraham totally bought into what God was doing, and that was the game-changer. He trusted God to make him right, instead of trying to earn it on his own."

Think of it like this: if you grind hard at a job, you earn your paycheck. That's not a gift, you earned it. But what if the job is way too big for you, like something only God could pull off? If you trust Him to handle it, knowing you could never do it yourself, that's what gets you right with God. It's a total gift, no strings attached.
King David even backs this up. He said the person who trusts God to wipe the slate clean, without trying to control everything, is super lucky:

> Lucky are the people whose crimes are whisked away,
> whose sins are wiped clean from the slate.
> Lucky is the person whose sin
> God doesn't even count.

Now, is this blessing only for the religious insiders, the ones who follow all the rules? Or can anyone get in on this? We all know Abraham was considered legit by God because he trusted God's plan, right?

And here's the thing: was Abraham declared legit *before* or *after* he went through the whole circumcision ceremony? That's right, it was *before*. The ceremony was just a sign, a confirmation of the faith he already had. It was proof that he was already on God's team.

This means Abraham is the father of *everyone* who trusts God, even if they're still considered "outsiders" and haven't gone through any religious rituals. They're the ones who get the "right with God" stamp of approval. And yeah, Abraham is also the father of the rule-followers, but not just because they checked a box. It's because they have the same kind of gutsy faith he did, way before he was officially marked.

That epic promise God made to Abraham—that his family would basically inherit the earth—wasn't because of anything Abraham did. It was all God's idea, and Abraham just had to trust it. If getting God's gifts was all about following a long list of rules and filling out paperwork, it would kill the whole trust thing and turn it into a business deal. That's not a promise; that's a contract with a bunch of fine print designed to trip you up. But with a promise, especially one from God, you can't break it.

That's why it all comes down to faith. God's promise is a pure gift, and that's how everyone gets in on it, whether you're a church kid or you've never even heard of this stuff. Abraham is the father of our faith, not our ancestor.

We call Abraham "father"—not our ancestor by blood, but the father of our faith—not because he was some perfect saint, but because God took a nobody and made him a somebody. Remember what God told him? "I'm making you the father of a huge family." Abraham was called a father *before* he even had kids because he dared to believe God could do the impossible, like bringing the dead back to life or creating something out of nothing. When everything looked hopeless, Abraham still believed. He chose to focus on what God *said* he would do, not on what he *couldn't* do. And that's how he became the father of a massive family.

Abraham didn't look at his 100-year-old body and say, "No way, I'm too old for this." He didn't look at his wife's infertility and give up. He didn't doubt God's promise. He went all-in, totally convinced that God would deliver. That's why the Bible says, "Abraham was made right with God because he trusted God." And it's not just about him; it's about us too! The same thing happens to us when we believe in the One who brought Jesus back from the dead when it seemed impossible. Jesus, the ultimate sacrifice, is the one who makes us right with God.

paragraphs: § Developing Patience

So, check it. Because we have faith, God's made us right with him. It's like we've leveled up our friendship with God, all thanks to our main man, Jesus. And it gets even better. We can now just walk right up to God, and he's already there with open arms. We're out in the wide-open spaces of God's grace and glory, standing tall and shouting out his praises.

But wait, there's more. We even shout praises when we're going through tough times. Why? Because we know that our struggles help us build up some serious patience. And that patience? It forges us into people with real character, always ready for what God's gonna do next. And with that kind of attitude, we're never let down. In fact, we can't even find enough words to describe how much awesome stuff God pours into our lives through the Holy Spirit.

Christ showed up right on time to make all this happen. He didn't wait for us to get our act together. He took one for the team and died for us when we were too weak and rebellious to do anything to help ourselves. I mean, we wouldn't have even known what to do. You might understand someone dying for a good person, someone who's worth it. But God put his love on full display for us by sending his Son to die for us while we were basically useless to him.

Now that we're good with God because of this ultimate sacrifice, there's no more beef between us. If we became friends with God when we were at our absolute worst, just imagine how much our lives are gonna change now that we're on his team! We've got this amazing friendship with God, and we're not just gonna talk about it in some boring way. We're gonna sing and shout our praises to God through Jesus, the Messiah!
§ The Death-Dealing Sin, the Life-Giving Gift

You know the story of how Adam messed things up for everyone. First came sin, then came death. Nobody was safe. That one mistake messed up our relationship with God, but nobody really knew how bad it was until God laid it all out for Moses. So, death was this giant canyon separating us from God, and it was like that from Adam all the way to Moses. Even people who didn't sin in the exact same way as Adam still had to deal with death and being separated from God. But Adam, the guy who got us into this mess, also points to the One who gets us out of it.

But the gift that saves us isn't like the sin that brought death. If one guy's mistake put a whole crowd of people in the timeout corner, separated from God, just think about what God's gift, given through one man, Jesus Christ, will do! You can't even compare the two. That one sin got a death sentence, but the gift that followed all the other sins was a life sentence—in a good way! If death was the boss because of one man's mess-up, imagine the epic comeback life makes for those who grab onto this crazy, extravagant gift of life and being made right with God, all provided by Jesus Christ.

Here's the short version: one person messed up and got us all into trouble with sin and death. Another person did everything right and got us out of it. But he didn't just get us out of trouble; he got us into a whole new life! One man told God, "Nah," and a lot of people got put in the wrong. One man told God, "Yes," and a lot of people were made right.

All those laws against sin just made more rule-breakers. But sin has no chance against the super-aggressive forgiveness we call grace. When it's sin vs. grace, grace wins, hands down. All sin can do is threaten us with death, and that's it. But grace, because God is putting everything back together through the Messiah, invites us into a life that just keeps going and going, forever and ever. Amen to that.

paragraphs: § When Death Becomes Life

So, what's the deal? Should we just keep messing up so God has to keep forgiving us? Like, racking up fouls because you know the ref will just keep calling them? No way, guy. That's a terrible strategy. If we've already ditched the world where sin is the boss, why would we keep a summer home there? Didn't you get the memo? We packed up and moved out for good. That's what baptism is all about. When you went under the water, you basically walked away from your old life of sin. When you came back up, you stepped into a whole new world, an incredible renewal powered by grace.

Being baptized into Jesus's crew is like this: going under the water is like being buried with him, and coming up is like his epic comeback, his resurrection. God the Father, in a massive power move, pulls us into this awesome new life so we can actually see where we're going. It's like getting a major life upgrade.

Let me break it down even more. Our old, cringey self was basically crucified with Christ. That whole miserable life where sin was calling the shots? It's over. Canceled. We're not stuck with its demands anymore. Here's the core belief: if we were part of Christ's death that totally owned sin, we're also part of his resurrection that gives us life. We know that when Jesus came back from the dead, it was the ultimate mic drop on death itself. Death doesn't get the final say anymore. When Jesus died, he took sin down with him. But now that he's alive, he connects us directly to God. So from now on, think of it like this: sin is a dead language, it's totally irrelevant to you. But God? He's speaking your language, and you should be hanging on every word. You're done with sin and totally alive for God. That's the life Jesus gives you—dead to sin and alive to God.

So, don't let sin have any say in how you live. Don't even give it the time of day. Don't do favors for that old, washed-up lifestyle. You've been raised from the dead, so go all-in on God's way of doing things. Sin can't be your boss anymore. You're not living under its miserable dictatorship. You're living in God's awesome freedom.
§ What Is True Freedom?

Now, what's real freedom? Are we supposed to just keep sinning because God forgives us? That's just wild. You can't keep living in sin and expect it to not catch up with you. If you hand yourself over to sin, it becomes your boss. But thank God you've started listening to a new master, one whose commands set you free to live openly in his freedom! If you follow God, you get freedom that never runs out.

Think about it: back when you did whatever you felt like, you thought you were free, but your freedom shrank. Remember how the more you just did what you felt like—not counting the cost, or the damage you did to others and to God—the less and less free you actually became? You were gradually becoming a slave to your own selfish habits, not thinking about how they hurt others or God, and you lost the ability to live free. And look at you now. You're a totally different person, and your life is wide open.

What did all that wild living get you? Back then, ignoring God, you didn't have to bother with right thinking or right living, or right anything. What was the payoff? Nothing you're proud of now. It was a dead end.

But now? You're free from all that mess. You're living for God, and the reward is eternal life. Working for sin? You get death. But God's gift? Real life, forever life, delivered by Jesus, our Master.

paragraphs: § Torn Between One Way and Another

Okay, real talk. You know how rules only apply to the living, right? Like, a married woman is bound to her husband while he's alive—if she goes off with another guy while he's still living, she's called an adulteress. But if her husband dies, she's not bound by the marriage rules anymore. She's free.

That's kinda what happened with us and the old rules. When Jesus died, he basically walked away from that whole system. Now we're free to be with him and produce something good for God. Before, when we were just doing whatever, we were trapped. Sin was the boss, and it was taking us down a dead end. But now, we've broken up with our toxic ex. We're done with those old rules. Now we can actually live for God, with his Spirit leading the way.

But wait, you're probably thinking, 'So the rules were bad?' Nah, not at all. The rules were actually super helpful. Without them, I wouldn't have even known what was wrong. Like, the rule 'Don't want what other people have'—if that wasn't a thing, I could've convinced myself that being jealous was a good look.

But sin is sneaky. Without all the fine print of the law code, sin looked pretty dull and lifeless, and I went along without paying much attention to it. But once sin got its hands on the law code and dressed itself up in all that finery, I was fooled, and I fell for it. It used that good rule and turned it into a temptation, like a 'forbidden fruit' situation. So the rule that was supposed to help me ended up tripping me up. Sin was having a party, and I was basically dead inside. The rules themselves are good, though. They're like God's common sense.

So, does that mean good things can hurt you? Nope. Sin is just a master manipulator. It used the good rules to trick me, making me think I could handle it, and then totally betrayed me. It used God's good rules as a disguise to do its dirty work.

I know God's commands are the real deal, but I'm just...not. I'm full of myself—after all, I've spent a long time in sin's prison. I'm a mess. I decide to do one thing, and then I do the complete opposite. I do stuff I totally hate. There's like a glitch in my system. So if I can't be trusted to figure out what's best for myself and then actually do it, it's obvious I need God's commands.

It's not really me; it's the sin living inside me. But I need something more! I know the law, but I still can't keep it, and the power of sin inside me keeps sabotaging my best intentions. I obviously need help! I want to do good, but I just can't. I can will it, but I can't do it. My decisions, such as they are, don't result in actions. Something deep inside me is sabotaging me every single time.

It's so predictable. I truly delight in God's commands, but it's pretty obvious not all of me joins in that delight. Every time I want to do the right thing, something inside me wants to do the opposite. It's like there's a secret rebel living in me that takes over when I least expect it.
I've tried everything, and nothing works. I'm at the end of my rope. Is there anyone who can help me? That's the real question, isn't it?

Thank God, the answer is yes! Jesus Christ. He's the one who can fix this mess. He's the one who helps me in this crazy life where I want to serve God with everything I have, but I'm constantly being pulled in a different direction by sin.

paragraphs: § The Solution Is Life on God's Terms

So, check it. When Jesus, the Messiah, showed up, he totally sorted out this massive problem we had. If you're on Team Jesus, you don't have to walk around under a dark cloud all the time. There's a new power in the game. The Holy Spirit, who brings life, has swooped in like a boss and totally cleared the air. You're free from being bossed around by sin and death.

God didn't mess around. He sent his own Son, Jesus, to deal with our messed-up situation head-on. Jesus became one of us, diving right into our chaotic lives to fix things for good. The old rules were like a weak Band-Aid on a massive wound – they just couldn't fix the deep problem of sin. But now, the Spirit is doing for us what we could never do for ourselves. We just have to trust him.

People who try to be good on their own are just flexing their moral muscles in the mirror but never actually doing anything. But if you trust God, his Spirit lives in you, and that's a total game-changer. Being self-obsessed is a dead end. Focusing on God is like stepping into an open world with no limits. If you're all about yourself, you're basically running off from God, and he's not a fan of that.

But if God is living in you, you're not thinking about yourself all the time. If someone doesn't have the Spirit of Christ, they're not on the team. But for you who have the Spirit, even though you still mess up, you're living on God's terms. And if the same God who brought Jesus back from the dead is living in you, he's going to give you a powerful shift and bring you to life too. With his Spirit in you, you're as alive as Christ!
So, you don't owe your old, selfish life anything. It's time to bury it and move on. God's Spirit is calling you to a new adventure.

This new life isn't about being scared and hiding. It's about being excited for what's next, like, 'What's up, Dad?' God's Spirit confirms that we're his kids. And as his kids, we get an awesome inheritance. We'll go through the tough stuff with Jesus, but we'll also get to share in the good times with him.

Honestly, the hard times we're going through now are nothing compared to the awesome future that's coming. The created world itself can hardly wait for what's coming next. Everything in creation is being more or less held back. God reins it in until both creation and all the creatures are ready, and then they can be released at the same moment into the glorious times ahead.

It's like the whole world is pregnant and about to give birth to something amazing. The Spirit of God is arousing us within. We're also feeling the birth pangs. These sterile and barren bodies of ours are yearning for full deliverance. And we feel it too. We're waiting for our own life-changing moment, to be totally free. Waiting doesn't make us weaker; it makes us stronger and more excited.

When we're tired of waiting, God's Spirit is right there to help us. When we don't know what to pray, he's got our back. He turns our groans into prayers. He knows us better than we know ourselves and makes sure we're good with God. That's why we can be sure that God works everything out for the best for those who love him.

God had a plan from the beginning. He decided to make us like his Son, Jesus. Jesus is the first in a new line of awesome humans. After God chose us, he called us, made us right with him, and he'll stick with us to the end. He's going to finish the amazing work he started in us.

So what's the takeaway? With God on our side, we can't lose. He gave up his own Son for us, so you know he's not going to hold back anything else from us. Who's going to mess with God's chosen people? Who's going to point a finger? Jesus died for us and came back to life, and right now he's in God's presence, sticking up for us. Nothing can separate us from Christ's love. Not trouble, not hard times, not hate, not hunger, not being homeless, not bullies, not backstabbers, not even the worst things you can imagine. Even when it feels like we're being taken out, none of it matters because Jesus loves us. I'm 100% sure that nothing – living or dead, angels or demons, today or tomorrow, high or low, anything you can think of – can get between us and God's love because of how Jesus has our back.

paragraphs: § God Is Calling His People

For real, I gotta tell you something that’s been weighing on me heavy. I’m not even capping, Jesus and the Holy Spirit know I’m telling the truth. I’m super bummed about my people, the Israelites. I’d totally take a massive L for them if it meant they could get a W with the Messiah. They’re my crew, my family. They had all the perks—the inside scoop on God, the promises, the sickest family tree that even led to Jesus, who is God over everything. They had everything going for them.

But don't get it twisted and think God's plan glitched or something. This has been the deal for a minute. Just 'cause you were born an Israelite doesn't mean you're automatically in God's inner circle. It was never about your bloodline, but about God's promise. Remember Abraham? God chose Isaac to be the one to carry on the family legacy, not just any of his kids. It was a God-pick, not a blood-pick. God was like, "Next year, Sarah's having a son, and he's the one."

And it wasn't a one-time thing. Check out what happened with Rebecca's twins, Jacob and Esau. Before they were even born, before they could do anything good or bad, God had already decided the older twin would be second fiddle to the younger one. God's plan isn't some random, hit-or-miss deal. He's the one calling the shots. He basically said, "Jacob's my boy, but I'm walking away from Esau."

So now you're probably thinking, "Whoa, that's not fair!" But hold up. God told Moses, "I show mercy to whoever I want to show mercy to." It's not about us trying to be good enough; it's all about God's mercy. He even told the Pharaoh that he was just a side character in God's big story of salvation. The point is, God makes the first move. He's the shot-caller.
And you can't just be like, 'Well, if God's in charge of everything, how can He blame us?'

Seriously, who are you to question God? Does a clay pot talk back to the potter and say, 'Why'd you make me look like this?' The potter can make whatever he wants with the clay—a fancy vase or a regular old pot. God can do the same thing. He can use some people to show his anger and others to show his amazing goodness. And this goes for everyone, not just the Israelites.

It's like the prophet Hosea said: God can take a bunch of nobodies and make them somebodies. He can take the unloved and make them loved. And where people were dissed as "nobodies," they'll be called "children of the living God." Isaiah looked ahead and spoke the truth: "If our powerful God had not provided us a legacy of living children, we would have ended up like ghost towns, like Sodom and Gomorrah." Isaiah also said that even if a ton of Israelites were chosen, only a few would actually be saved. God doesn't just count heads; He calls us by name. It's personal.

So, here's the deal. The non-Israelites, who weren't even trying to get right with God, ended up getting right with Him because they trusted Him. But the Israelites, who were all about the rules and trying to do everything right, totally missed the point. Why? Because they were trying to do it all themselves instead of just trusting God. They were so focused on their own projects that they didn't even see God standing right in front of them, like a giant rock in the road. And they tripped right over Him. It's like Isaiah said: "Watch out, I'm putting a huge stone in your path. But that stone is me. If you're looking for me, you'll find me."

title: The Ultimate Cheat Code

paragraphs: § Israel Reduced to Religion

For real, all I want is for my people, the Israelites, to be saved. I'm praying for it 24/7. They're super passionate about God, I'll give them that, but they're going about it all wrong. They're trying to earn their way to God by following a bunch of rules, like it's a DIY project. They've set up their own little 'salvation stores' selling fakes, when God's got the real deal right there. They've been trying to do it their own way for ages, and they've got nothing to show for it.

The whole point of the old rules was to get everyone ready for Jesus. He's the one who makes everything right with God for anyone who trusts in him. Moses even said that trying to be perfect by following all the rules is a total grind. But trusting God is a whole different story. You don't have to do some epic quest to find Jesus; he's right here. The secret sauce is super simple. Just say it out loud: "Jesus is the boss." And believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead. That's it. You're not earning your way to heaven; you're just trusting God to do the heavy lifting. That's how you get saved. When you believe it in your heart and say it with your mouth, you're in.

The old book says that anyone who trusts in God will never be let down. And it doesn't matter who you are or where you come from. God's the same for everyone, and he's super generous to everyone who asks for his help. If you call on God, he'll be there for you.

But how can people ask for help if they don't know who to ask? And how can they know who to ask if nobody tells them? And how can anyone tell them unless someone is sent? That's why the old book says that people who share the good news are a beautiful sight. But not everyone's ready to listen. The prophet Isaiah even asked, "God, is anyone even listening?" So, you have to hear the message before you can believe it. And there's no message to hear unless someone is talking about Jesus.

And for real, Israel has had plenty of chances to hear the message. The good news has been preached all over the world. So why didn't they get it? Moses knew what was up. He said that when they saw God helping out people they thought were outsiders, they'd get super jealous. And when they saw God being cool with people they thought were clueless, they'd throw a fit. Then Isaiah just came out and said it: God found people who weren't even looking for him. And then he said that he reached out to Israel day after day, and all he got back was silence.

paragraphs: § The Loyal Minority

So, does this mean God's totally done with Israel? Like, he's walking away from them for good? No way. Don't forget, I'm an Israelite myself, a descendant of Abraham from the tribe of Benjamin. You can't get more legit than that. So, God's not ditching his people. He's been with them for way too long and has invested too much to just walk away.

Remember that time Elijah was complaining to God about Israel? He was all like, "God, they took out your prophets and wrecked your altars. I'm the only one left, and now they're coming for me!" And what did God say back? "I've still got a 7,000-person deep crew who are ride-or-die." It's the same deal today. There's a small but super-loyal group still hanging on. They're not in it for what they can get; they're just all-in on God's grace and his plan. If it was just about them, they would've bounced a long time ago.

So what's the deal? When Israel tried to do things their own way, they failed. The real chosen ones were the ones who let God do his thing in them, and they got his seal of approval. The rest of them just got stubborn and closed off to God. Moses and Isaiah even called it out, saying God basically let them go away in their own hype. And David said he hoped they'd get sick of their own selfish ways.
§ Pruning and Grafting Branches

So, are they out for the count? Is it game over for them? Not a chance. It's actually pretty wild because when they walked away, it opened the door for everyone else to come in. And now, seeing all these outsiders join the party, the Israelites are starting to feel a little jealous. If them leaving caused this huge wave of people to come to God, imagine what will happen when they come back! It's gonna be epic.

I'm telling you this because my job is to bring in the outsiders. But I'm also hoping that my own people, the insiders, will see what's happening and want back in. If them messing up led to something good for you, think about how awesome it'll be when they get it right. It's gonna be a massive homecoming.

Think of it like this: there's a super-strong, God-planted root. If the root is legit, the fruit's gonna be fire. Some of the OG branches got snipped, and you guys, who were like wild weeds, got grafted in. But don't get it twisted—you're getting your life from that root, not the other way around. So don't go flexing on the branches that got cut.
You might be thinking, 'Well, they got cut so I could get in!' True, but they got cut because they were dead weight and you got in because you trusted God. So don't get cocky. Stay humble.

If God didn't hesitate to snip the original branches, he won't think twice about you. He's both super kind and super strict. He's ruthless with the dead weight but gentle with the new growth. But don't take his kindness for granted. The second you become dead weight, it's game over.

And don't feel all high and mighty about the branches on the ground. If they stop being dead weight, they can get grafted right back in. God can do that. If he can take you from the wild and graft you into his tree, he can definitely put the original branches back where they belong. Just be glad you're in the tree and hope for the best for everyone else.
§ A Complete Israel

I'm laying it all out for you because it's complicated, and I don't want you to get the wrong idea and think you're all that and they're nothing. That's not it at all. Israel's current cold shoulder towards God is just temporary. It's to make room for all the outsiders, so we can have a full house. In the end, all of Israel will be back together. Like the old-school prophets said: A hero's gonna roll in from Zion and totally clean house. And God promised to take away their sins.
From your perspective, it might look like the Jews are God's enemies. But from God's long-term view, they're still his oldest friends. God's gifts and his call are for life—no take-backs.

Not long ago, you were the ones on the outs with God. But then the Jews slammed the door on him, and that opened things up for you. Now they're on the outs, but because the door is wide open for you, they have a way back in. God makes sure everyone knows what it's like to be on the outside so he can be the one to welcome us all back in.

Have you ever seen anything as awesome as God's generosity and wisdom? It's totally next-level. We'll never fully get it. Who can explain God? Who's smart enough to tell him what to do? Who's ever done him a favor so big that God owes them? Everything comes from him, happens through him, and ends up in him. All the glory and praise to him, always. Yes. Yes. Yes.

paragraphs: § Place Your Life Before God

Alright, so here's the deal. God's got your back, so listen up. Your everyday life—the whole routine of waking up, eating, going to school, and just hanging out—give it all to God. It's like a thank-you gift. The best thing you can do for Him is to just accept all the awesome stuff He does for you. Don't just blend in with everyone else and do what they do without thinking. That's no way to live. Instead, focus on God. He'll give you an amazing change from the inside out. You'll start to see what He wants, and you'll actually want to do it. The world will try to drag you down to its level, but God? He'll make you the best version of yourself. He'll help you level up.

I'm telling you this because I'm super grateful for everything God's given me, and I feel like I owe it to you guys. We're all living on God's positive energy, so don't get it twisted and think you're the one doing all the good stuff. Nah, that's all God. The only way to really get who you are is to see who God is and what He does for you, not what you do for Him.

Think of it like this: we're all different parts of a body. Each part is important, but only because it's part of the whole body. That body is Team Jesus. We all have our own special thing to do as part of His crew. A finger or a toe by itself is pretty useless, right? So since we're all part of this awesome, well-oiled machine that is Team Jesus, let's just be who we were made to be. No need to get jealous or braggy, or try to be someone you're not.

If your thing is to speak up for God, then just do that. Don't add a bunch of your own stuff. If you're a helper, then just help, don't try to take over. If you're a teacher, then stick to teaching. If you're good at giving advice, don't be a bossy know-it-all. If you're in charge, don't be a manipulator. If you're supposed to help people who are struggling, then be ready to jump in and help. If you're working with people who have it rough, don't get all annoyed or bummed out by them. Just keep a smile on your face.

Love people for real, from the heart. Don't be a fake. Run from bad stuff like it's on fire, and hold on to good stuff for dear life. Be a true friend who loves big. And hey, it's cool to let someone else be the star sometimes.

Don't get lazy. Stay fired up and ready to go. Be on the lookout for ways to serve the big Boss. Be excited about what's coming. When things get tough, don't give up—just pray even harder. Help out other Christians who are in need. Get creative with being welcoming.

If people are hating on you, wish them well. Don't be cursing them out when no one's listening. When your friends are happy, be happy with them. When they're sad, be sad with them. Just get along with everyone. Don't be a snob. Make friends with the nobodies, and don't try to be some big shot important person.

Don't get revenge. Try to see the good in everyone. As much as you can, just chill with everybody. Don't be the one to try and get even. That's not your job. God says, "I'm the judge. I'll handle it."

It's like the old stories say: if your enemy is hungry, buy them a burger. If they're thirsty, get them a Coke. Your kindness will totally blow their mind. Don't let evil win. Beat evil by doing good.

paragraphs: § To Be a Responsible Citizen

Alright, listen up. You gotta play by the rules. All the people in charge, like the government and stuff? God put them there. As long as things are peaceful and not totally chaotic, that's God's doing. So, be a good citizen. If you're a pain to the government, you're basically dissing God, and He's not gonna let that slide. The authorities are only a problem if you're trying to pull a fast one. If you're just living your life, you've got nothing to worry about.

Want to stay on the government's good side? It's easy: just be a responsible person. They'll even help you out. But if you're out there breaking all the rules, you better watch your back. The cops aren't just for show; God uses them to keep things in order. That's why you gotta live right—not just 'cause you're scared of getting busted, but because it's the right thing to do.
That's also why you have to pay taxes. It's so we can have a decent society. So, pay your taxes, pay your bills, and give a little respect to the people in charge.

Look, don't owe anyone anything, except for the massive debt of love you have for each other. When you love other people, you're basically nailing what the law is all about. All those rules—don't cheat, don't kill, don't steal, don't be jealous of what other people have—they all boil down to one thing: love other people as much as you love yourself. You can't mess up when you're showing love. It's the ultimate cheat code.

But for real, don't get so caught up in your day-to-day grind that you forget what time it is. The world as we know it is almost over; a new day is coming. So, wake up and see what God's up to! He's putting the final touches on the incredible renewal he started in us when we first believed. We can't waste a single second. Don't get involved in hooking up and partying recklessly, don't get involved in fighting and petty jealousies. Get up, get dressed in Christ, and let's get going!

paragraphs: § Cultivating Good Relationships

Alright, so check it. When someone new joins the squad, and they're not quite on the same page as you about everything, don't just roast them. Welcome them in. Don't start a whole debate every time they do something you think is weird. They've got their own stuff to figure out, so just be cool.

For real, some people who've been around for a bit are like, "I can eat whatever I want, it's all good." Then you've got others who are like, "Nah, I'm sticking to veggies only." And you know what? Both are cool. They're both guests at Christ's table. It would be terrible to start hating on what someone else is or isn't eating. God invited them, so who are you to kick them out? If they need to learn some manners, God's got it covered. He doesn't need your help to be the hall monitor.

Same thing with special days. Some people think certain days are a big deal, like a holiday, and others think every day is pretty much the same. There are good reasons for both. So, you do you. Follow what your conscience tells you.

Here's the deal: if you're treating a day like it's special, do it for God. If you're chowing down on a burger, do it for God and be thankful. If you're a vegetarian, eat your salad for God and be thankful. It's not about you. It's God we are answerable to—all the way from life to death and everything in between—not each other. That's why Jesus lived and died and then lived again: so he could be our Master across the entire range of life and death, and free us from the petty tyrannies of each other.

So, what's the point of dissing your friends? Or acting like you're better than them? It just makes you look silly. One day, we're all going to be in front of God, and all that trash talk isn't going to help you. It's like the Bible says, "Every single person will bow down to me, and everyone will admit that I'm God." So, mind your own business. You've got enough on your plate just dealing with your own life.

Forget about being the judge of what's right for everyone else. Just worry about not messing things up for other people. Don't be a stumbling block. I'm 100% sure—Jesus convinced me—that everything in itself is holy. But we can make it bad by how we act or talk about it.

If you're making a big deal about what someone eats and it's causing drama, you're not being a good friend. Remember, Jesus died for them too. Would you risk wrecking them completely over a slice of pizza? Don't you dare let a piece of God-blessed food become an occasion of soul-poisoning!

God's kingdom isn't about what's on your plate. It's about how God is working in your life, making you a better person, and filling you with joy. Your job is to serve Christ. If you do that, you'll be good with God and people will respect you.

So, let's all just try to get along. Build each other up, don't tear each other down. Don't let an argument over dinner wreck the amazing things God is doing. All food is fine, but it's not fine if you use it to trip someone up. When you're eating with people, think about sharing the life of Jesus, not just your own stomach. Be cool, be respectful, and don't do anything that gets in the way of love.

Keep your own relationship with God strong, but don't force it on other people. You're in a good spot if what you believe and how you act line up. But if you're not sure, and you're acting one way one day and another way the next, you're out of line. If your life doesn't match your beliefs, then something's wrong.

paragraphs: Alright, so for those of us who are solid in our faith, we gotta help out the ones who are still a bit shaky. It's not about what's easy for us; it's about having their backs. Strength isn't for showing off, it's for serving. We should all be looking out for each other and asking, "Hey, how can I help?"

That's exactly what Jesus did. He didn't just walk away from everyone's problems; he jumped right in the middle of the mess to help out. Like the old-school texts say, "I took on the troubles of the troubled." And yeah, even though that was written ages ago, it's for us. God wants the combo of his steady, constant calling and his warm, personal counsel in Scripture to shape who we are, keeping us sharp and ready for whatever he's gonna do next. Hopefully, our awesome God will help you guys mature and get along, just like Jesus gets along with everyone. Then, we'll be like a massive choir, our lives singing a fire anthem to God.

So, welcome everyone, no drama. Jesus did it, so now it's our turn. He reached out to the Jews to make good on the promises made to their ancestors. And because of that, everyone else got to experience God's mercy and give Him a shout-out. Think about all the old prophecies coming true because of what we're doing! Like these:

"I'll sing with the outsiders, I'll shout out your name!"

And this one:

"Outsiders and insiders, let's party together!"

And another one:

"Everyone, from every country, celebrate God! All you people, give Him a huge round of applause!"

And what Isaiah said:

"A new branch will grow from Jesse's family tree, and it'll be so tall that everyone, everywhere, can see it and have hope!"
So, may the God of hope fill you up with so much joy and peace that your believing lives, filled with the life-giving energy of the Holy Spirit, brim over with hope!

Personally, I'm really proud of you guys. You're all doing great, you've got good hearts, and you know your stuff. You're totally capable of giving each other good advice. So don't think I'm roasting you with my blunt words. I'm just saying I need your help with this special mission God gave me: to be a spiritual guide for the non-Jews, so they can be presented as an acceptable offering to God, made whole and holy by God's Holy Spirit.

Looking back, I'm pretty stoked about what we've accomplished with Jesus. I'm not here to tell you some crazy adventure story, but to tell you how Christ's power in me made the outsiders believe. I've been spreading the message of Jesus from Jerusalem all the way to Greece, like a pioneer in places where no one had even heard of Him. My motto has been: "Those who were never told about him will see him! And those who've never heard will finally get the message!"

And that's why it's taken me so long to come see you. But now that my work here is done, and I've been wanting to visit you for years, I'm making plans. I'm heading to Spain and I'll stop by to hang out with you all. Hopefully, you'll send me off with God's blessing.

But first, I've gotta go to Jerusalem to drop off some donations for the believers there. The Greeks, from Macedonia to Achaia, all pitched in to help the poor in Jerusalem. They were happy to do it, and it was the right thing to do. Since they've benefited so much from the spiritual gifts from Jerusalem, it's only fair they help out with their money. As soon as I've delivered this gift, I'm off to Spain, with a stop in Rome to see you. I'm hoping my visit will be a huge blessing from Christ.

Please pray for me, guys. Pray strenuously with and for me—to God the Father, through the power of our Master Jesus, through the love of the Spirit—that I'll be delivered from the lions' den of unbelievers in Judea. And pray that the believers in Jerusalem will accept the gift I'm bringing. Then, if it's God's will, I'll come to you with a happy heart, ready to be refreshed by your company. May God's peace be with all of you. Amen.

paragraphs: Hey, check it out. First up, I want you to give a massive welcome to our friend Phoebe. She's a key representative of the church over in Cenchrea. I heartily endorse both her and her work. Roll out the red carpet for her, show her some major love, and help her with whatever she asks. She deserves anything you can do for her. Seriously, she's the real deal and has been a huge help to a ton of people, including me.

Next, big shout-out to Priscilla and Aquila, my partners in crime for Jesus. These two are legit heroes—they literally put their lives on the line for me. I'm not the only one who's grateful; all the non-Jewish churches owe them big time. And what's super cool is they host a church right in their own house. Talk about squad goals! Give a holler to my boy Epenetus, the very first person in Asia to jump on board with Team Jesus.
And a huge thank you to Mary, who has worked her tail off for us. What a legend!
What up to my relatives Andronicus and Junias! We were cellmates back in the day, and they were followers of Christ even before I was. These two are some of the most respected leaders out there.
Shout-out to my good friend Ampliatus, part of God's family.
And to Urbanus, our teammate in Christ's work, and my man Stachys.
Props to Apelles, a true veteran who's been tested and proven in his walk with Christ. And a big hello to the whole crew at Aristobulus's house.
Hey to my cousin Herodion! And to all the believers in Narcissus's household.
What's good, Tryphena and Tryphosa? These ladies are always hustling for the Lord. And another shout-out to my dear friend Persis, who's also a super hard worker for Christ.
Say hi to Rufus—a really good choice by the Master—and to his mom, who's been like a second mom to me.
And what's up to Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermes, Patrobas, Hermas, and all their families?
And to Philologus, Julia, Nereus and his sister, and Olympas, and all the other followers of Jesus living with them.
Basically, give everyone a big ol' holy hug. All the churches of Christ are sending you their love!

Now, for a final word of advice, my friends. Keep your eyes peeled for people who try to stir up trouble and mess with the truth you've learned. These guys are fakes. They're not serving our main man, Jesus; they're just in it for themselves. They'll use smooth talk and fake piety to trick people who don't know any better. So, give them a wide berth and don't get played.

I'm so proud of you guys because you're known for being the real deal. But I also want you to be street smart. Know the difference between what's good and what's just a good-looking fake. Don't be naive when it comes to evil. Stay sharp, and before you know it, the God of peace will totally crush Satan under your feet. Enjoy all the good stuff Jesus has for you!
Oh, and a few more shout-outs from my end. Timothy, my right-hand man, says hi. So do Lucius and my cousins Jason and Sosipater.
And from me, Tertius, the guy who actually wrote this letter down for Paul, I'm sending you my own personal hello!
Gaius, who's been an awesome host to me and the whole church here, sends his greetings. And so do Erastus, the city's finance director, and our good buddy Quartus.

So, let's give all the praise to the One who has the power to make you strong. This is the same message I've been preaching about Jesus Christ. For ages, it was a secret, but now the secret's out! Thanks to the ancient prophets, the master plan has been revealed. Now, people from all over the world can hear the truth, believe, and get on board with God's plan. This was all God's idea, from start to finish.
All the glory and praise go to the one and only wise God, through Jesus Christ. Amen! High five!
